**What the reports cover (brief summary of the most recent one)**  

- **Report 23‑00116‑148 (2024)** – A Comprehensive Healthcare Inspection of the Boise VA Medical Center. The inspection evaluated the facility’s overall compliance with VA health‑care standards, identified several findings (e.g., gaps in patient‑safety processes, documentation, and oversight), and issued recommendations for corrective action. The report includes a full list of findings, the facility’s response, and target dates for implementation.  

- **Report 16‑00557‑134 (2017)** – A Clinical Assessment Program (CAP) review that examined clinical operations at the Boise VA Medical Center, noting strengths and weaknesses in patient care, staffing, and quality‑improvement processes.  

- **Report 13‑04241‑78 (2014)** – A Combined Assessment Program review that provided an overall assessment of the Boise VA Medical Center’s compliance with VA policies and identified areas for improvement.  

- **Report 13‑04331‑63 (2014)** – Reviews of the Community‑Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC) and Primary Care Clinic at the Boise VA Medical Center, focusing on outpatient services, patient access, and care coordination.  

- **Report 16‑04762‑232 (2017)** – An inspection of the VA Regional Office (VARO) for Boise, Idaho, which included recommendations to strengthen the claims‑establishment review process and provide refresher training for staff.

### Summary (quoted)

> “This Office of Inspector General (OIG) Comprehensive Healthcare Inspection Program report describes the results of a focused evaluation of the quality of care delivered in the inpatient and outpatient settings of the Boise VA Medical Center and multiple outpatient clinics in Idaho and Oregon. This evaluation focused on five key operational areas:  
> • Leadership and organizational risks  
> • Quality, safety, and value  
> • Medical staff privileging  
> • Environment of care  
> • Mental health (suicide prevention initiatives)  
> The OIG issued four recommendations for improvement in two areas:  
> 1. Environment of care – Inpatient Psychiatry Unit panic and over‑the‑door alarm testing  
> 2. Mental health – Monthly reporting of suicide‑related events to mental health leaders and quality management staff; Comprehensive Suicide Risk Evaluation completion.”  

*(source: `summary` field)*

## Findings & Recommendations (quoted)

### 1. Environment of Care – Panic Alarm Testing (Inpatient Psychiatry Unit)  
- **Finding (text)**: “The Medical Center Director ensures staff document VA police response times to panic alarm testing in the Inpatient Psychiatry Unit.”  
- **Recommendation (rec 1)**:  
  > “The Medical Center Director and the facility Chief, Police Service evaluated the finding… implemented a new process to document Veterans Administration Police response times on an Inpatient Psychiatry Unit panic alarm response time tracking log. In March 2024, the facility Accreditation Manager will initiate monthly auditing to monitor compliance… Goal = ≥ 90 % compliance, sustained for six consecutive months. Results reported to the Quality and Safety Council.”  
- **Status**: closed‑implemented (target date 2024‑10‑31).  

### 2. Environment of Care – Over‑the‑Door Alarm Maintenance  
- **Finding (text)**: “The Medical Center Director ensures staff follow the manufacturer’s guidelines for checking over‑the‑door alarms for patient sleeping rooms in the Inpatient Psychiatry Unit.”  
- **Recommendation (rec 2)**:  
  > “Updated the electronic preventive maintenance system to generate work orders for monthly preventive maintenance of over‑the‑door alarms… Auditing to monitor compliance → goal ≥ 90 % sustained for six months. Results reported to Quality and Safety Council.”  
- **Status**: closed‑implemented (target date 2024‑10‑31).

### 3. Mental Health – Suicide‑Related Event Reporting  
- **Finding (text)**: “The Medical Center Director ensures the Suicide Prevention Coordinator reports suicide‑related events to mental health leaders and quality management staff at least monthly.”  
- **Recommendation (rec 3)**:  
  > “Suicide Prevention Coordinator implemented monthly reporting of suicide‑related event data to the Quality and Safety Council and Behavioral Health Leadership. Two monthly audits were started in October 2023 to monitor compliance. Goal ≥ 90 % compliance for six consecutive months; quarterly reporting to Quality and Safety Council.”  
- **Status**: closed‑implemented (target date 2024‑10‑31).

### 4. Mental Health – Comprehensive Suicide Risk Evaluation Completion  
- **Finding (text)**: “The Medical Center Director ensures providers complete the Comprehensive Suicide Risk Evaluation following a patient’s positive suicide risk screen.”  
- **Recommendation (rec 4)**:  
  > “Developed single‑point lesson documents and face‑to‑face/self‑directed training (June‑August 2023). In April 2024, a pop‑up notification and real‑time report will enable daily compliance monitoring. Audits to achieve ≥ 90 % compliance, sustained for two consecutive quarters; quarterly reporting to Quality and Safety Council.”  
- **Status**: closed‑implemented (target date 2024‑12‑31).
